atomic_claim: Server initializes SQLite runtime state before the engine and hydrates catalog/snapshots/history through the runtime repository.
notes: State is durable when catalog_db points to a file.

atomic_claim: Persisted identity maps are synchronized into the engine at startup.
notes: Provider registry records do not receive equivalent runtime activation.

atomic_claim: GET /health reports server and engine status plus table/context/control-plane counts.
notes: API is unversioned.

atomic_claim: POST /query executes ContextQL through the core engine and returns JSON rows and metadata.
notes: Only JSON response format is implemented.

atomic_claim: SELECT requests require an explicit LIMIT no greater than the configured maximum.
notes: DDL and catalog statements bypass this check by design.

atomic_claim: Engine execution is configured with a maximum intermediate-row ceiling.
notes: Core engine supplies the pre-materialization enforcement.

atomic_claim: Encoded query responses are rejected when they exceed the configured byte ceiling.
notes: Enforcement occurs after result construction.

atomic_claim: POST /query/explain executes the query and returns actual rows plus the engine trace.
notes: This is not a dry explain and may conflict with whitepaper plan-only semantics.

atomic_claim: Explain traces expose resolved contexts provider calls identity-map names and score breakdown.
notes: Evidence-level membership explanations are not a distinct API.

atomic_claim: POST /contexts creates a durable context through executable ContextQL DDL and then assigns draft state.
notes: Core CREATE initially creates active before the service changes it to draft.

atomic_claim: Context list and describe APIs return the latest non-dropped version with namespace and lifecycle filters.
notes: No authorization filtering is applied.

atomic_claim: Context updates are expressed as ALTER CONTEXT operations and force the latest definition to draft.
notes: Request fields entity_key has_score and classification are accepted by the model but not applied by service.update.

atomic_claim: The server exposes validate activate and retire transitions over a four-state lifecycle.
notes: The nine-state whitepaper lifecycle and query-time state gating are not implemented.

atomic_claim: Deletion is allowed only when the latest context version is in draft state.
notes: DROP semantics also depend on core dependency handling.

atomic_claim: The server exposes all stored context versions in ascending version order.
notes: No dedicated diff endpoint is present.

atomic_claim: The preview API executes a context definition and returns a bounded sample while recording execution metadata.
notes: Preview executes definition SQL; it is not a static plan operation.

atomic_claim: The refresh API executes REFRESH CONTEXT through the engine and returns updated catalog state.
notes: Failure state is recorded in runtime metadata.

atomic_claim: Snapshot and membership-history APIs expose persisted context runtime state.
notes: History query authorization and classification filtering are absent.

atomic_claim: Three SQLite migrations define catalog provider identity audit snapshot payload history and connector synchronization state.
notes: Migrations use sequential ALTER statements and require upgrade testing.

atomic_claim: Snapshot publication persists payload checksums metadata current/superseded state and history in a transaction.
notes: SQLite is the only persistent backend.

atomic_claim: Runtime hydration verifies payload checksums and fails closed on corruption.
notes: No automated repair path is provided.

atomic_claim: Refresh publication preserves the old current snapshot until the replacement is durably promoted.
notes: Concurrency guarantee is scoped to the SQLite/reference runtime.

atomic_claim: An optional background scheduler refreshes due active contexts and records refresh failures.
notes: This is not the whitepaper's full distributed scheduler/resource governor.

atomic_claim: The provider registry durably stores MCP/REMOTE metadata lifecycle and health fields.
notes: Credentials are stored as references.

atomic_claim: Provider CRUD enable disable and health APIs are available.
notes: Health endpoint returns stored state rather than actively probing an endpoint.

atomic_claim: Persisted provider records are not automatically instantiated or registered with the core engine.
notes: Built-in/mock providers are registered through separate startup code.

atomic_claim: Identity map metadata is persisted and synchronized to the engine at startup.
notes: Only registration/list/describe APIs are present.

atomic_claim: The server model records matching mode and confidence but the runtime sync registers path pairs only.
negative_evidence: No probabilistic matching or global canonical entity namespace is implemented.
notes: Metadata maturity exceeds execution semantics.

atomic_claim: Mutation query lifecycle and server events can be appended to a filterable SQLite audit log.
notes: Append-only behavior is a service convention rather than a database immutability control.

atomic_claim: Audit records are not hash chained signed or protected by authorization.
negative_evidence: No hash-chain/RBAC enforcement code is present.
notes: Whitepaper regulated-industry claims exceed this maturity.

atomic_claim: The server has no authentication RBAC RLS or tenant-enforcement middleware.
negative_evidence: No authentication dependency or permission check is wired into routes.
notes: Namespace and classification are metadata not access controls.

atomic_claim: DeepSee client supports credential resolution bounded retry/backoff timeout and response validation.
notes: Connector is vendor-specific reference integration.

atomic_claim: DeepSee MCP provider supports id-list and Roaring64 bitmap membership with pagination watermarks scores and evidence references.
notes: Pagination is bounded by a maximum-page guard.

atomic_claim: DeepSee REMOTE provider supplies bounded relational evidence resources and rejects rows outside requested entity filters.
notes: Only two modeled resources are supported.

atomic_claim: DeepSee synchronizer supports bootstrap incremental folding idempotency durable watermarks and failure-safe publication.
notes: A generic federation broker/scheduler contract is not present.

atomic_claim: Server version metadata is inconsistent across package and application surfaces.
negative_evidence: Package/README say v0.1 while FastAPI and audit startup report 0.3.0.
notes: Requires adjudication rather than an automatic version bump.
